data.title: Tandem forecasts $265M Q3 sales while advancing Mobi tubeless scaled launch in H2 2026
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Tandem Diabetes Care (TNDM) Q2 2026

Management View

  • “The second quarter marked an important step forward for Tandem. We are executing against our strategic priorities while demonstrating operational momentum, improving our financial performance, and providing broader access to our technology.” (President, CEO & Director John Sheridan)
  • “We now have approximately 45% formulary coverage, which is already approaching the high end of our range for the goals this year.” (President Sheridan)
  • “In our first full quarter offering PAYGO, U.S. sales through the pharmacy channel increased to 10%.” (President Sheridan)
  • “We reached an important R&D milestone in Q2 with a 510(k) submission for Mobi tubeless.” (President Sheridan)
  • “To support this, we are launching AutoSoft Plus… and plan to expand to additional geographies, including the U.S. later this year.” (President Sheridan)
  • “Over the past 2 years… culminating in FDA approval of an IDE in Q2 and positioning us to begin a pivotal study later this year.” (President Sheridan)
  • “Worldwide sales totaled $255 million, increasing 6% year-over-year or 5% in constant currency.” (Executive VP, CFO & Treasurer Leigh Vosseller)
  • “Gross margin was 57%, improving 5 percentage points year-over-year and 2 points sequentially.” (Executive VP Vosseller)

Outlook

  • “For the third quarter, worldwide sales are expected to be approximately $265 million.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “Worldwide sales are expected to be in the range of $1.065 billion to $1.085 billion.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “We expect gross margins in the range of 56% to 57% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 5% to 6% of annual sales.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “Gross margin is expected to be approximately 56% and adjusted EBITDA margin approximately 2% of sales.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • Compared with Q1, management again “reaffirm[ed]” full-year sales and margin guidance, while Q2 commentary emphasized that PAYGO is in its “first full quarter” with “sales through the pharmacy… 10%,” versus Q1’s description of early weeks where “Fewer than 5% of customers ordered a pump through their pharmacy benefit.” (Executive VP Vosseller)

Financial Results

  • “We shipped approximately 33,000 pumps worldwide.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “In the U.S., we shipped a Q2 record of 22,000 pumps, growing 7% year-over-year.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “In the second quarter, the initial headwind from pharmacy pumps was approximately $8 million.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “International sales totaled $75 million, increasing 7% year-over-year or 6% in constant currency.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “Operating expenses were $159 million, remaining relatively flat year-over-year.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “We ended the quarter with a healthy balance sheet including $456 million in cash and investments compared to $570 million at the end of Q1.” (Executive VP Vosseller)

Q&A

  • Mathew Blackman, TD Cowen: asked about “areas… of friction in the pharmacy transition” and confidence in targets for “20% of pump shipments through the pharmacy.” President Sheridan: “there was nothing that was surprising. We feel like we're on track.”
  • Felipe Lamar, Truist: asked about “retention issues in the Type 2 community.” President Sheridan: “our Type 2 attrition, it's really modestly higher than our Type 1 rate, and it's been stable over the past 5 years.”
  • Larry Biegelsen, Wells Fargo: pressed on second-half drivers to hit U.S. pump guidance. Executive VP Vosseller: “we have a number of new products under launch right now… FreeStyle Libre 3… Mobi Android… pharmacy.”
  • Matthew O’Brien, Piper Sandler: asked why gross margin guide was reiterated and why Q3 steps down. Executive VP Vosseller: “we guided to a point step down in Q3, but still achieving that 60% gross margin in the fourth quarter.”
  • Joanne Wuensch, Citi: asked whether tubeless Mobi was filed and timing. President Sheridan: “we have filed it… we are planning on having clearance and actually beginning the scaling launch in the second half of this year.”
  • Jonathan Block, Stifel: asked whether higher pharmacy pricing implied supply conversions lagging. Executive VP Vosseller: “the pump adoption slightly outpaced… the supply side… that may continue into the third quarter.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing around execution risk and pacing, including “friction in the pharmacy transition,” implied shipment softness, and whether pharmacy conversion cadence is realistic.
  • Management’s tone was slightly positive and confident, repeatedly using conviction language such as “we feel like we're on track” and “we remain confident,” while acknowledging operational pacing effects like “pump adoption… outpaced… the supply side.”
  • Versus Q1’s early-stage framing (“still early in the process”), Q2 kept a similar confidence level but leaned more on tangible traction (“sales through the pharmacy… 10%”) and reiterated margin pathway (“still achieving that 60% gross margin in the fourth quarter”).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • PAYGO progressed from Q1’s “Fewer than 5%” pharmacy pump and supply adoption to Q2’s “sales through the pharmacy increased to 10%,” alongside formulary coverage moving from “approximately 40%” to “approximately 45%.” (Executive VP Vosseller; Executive VP Vosseller; President Sheridan)
  • Tubeless Mobi moved from Q1 planning (“We plan to file our 510(k) submission… in the second quarter”) to Q2 completion (“a 510(k) submission for Mobi tubeless”). (President Sheridan)
  • International go-direct messaging stayed consistent, but Q2 highlighted incremental timing headwinds (“$3 million… distributor inventory buybacks”) versus Q1 discussing timing of go-direct headwinds shifting into Q2. (Executive VP Vosseller)

Risks and Concerns

  • “We continue to manage shortages from our key infusion set supplier. We believe Q2 was the period of greatest impact, and our supplier expects availability to improve through the second half of the year.” (President Sheridan)
  • “Pump shipments through the pharmacy channels do not include upfront reimbursement, which creates a near-term headwind to revenue.” (Executive VP Vosseller)
  • “There’s still uncertainty from the FDA” on tubeless Mobi timing, with launch described as a “scaled launch” in the second half. (President Sheridan)

Final Takeaway

Management characterized Q2 as a step-up in execution, highlighting PAYGO traction (10% pharmacy mix and 45% formulary coverage), gross margin expansion to 57%, and a filed 510(k) for Mobi tubeless ahead of a planned scaled launch in the second half of 2026. Leadership also reaffirmed full-year sales and margin ranges while flagging near-term headwinds from pharmacy accounting dynamics and infusion-set supply constraints that they expect to ease through the second half.

data.title: Weak jobs report backs Fed pause as inflation takes center stage, Kelly and Hatzius - CNBC
data.description:
July's weak jobs report supported a Fed pause, while inflation remained the key policy driver, David Kelly and Jan Hatzius said in separate CNBC interviews.

Hatzius called the payrolls report “weaker” overall, saying Goldman Sachs' composite measure of underlying job growth had slowed to about 5K from just over 70K before the report after incorporating the latest data and revisions.

"The biggest takeaway" was the sharp slowdown in underlying job growth, Hatzius said. While the household survey was more mixed, he said recent declines in labor force participation suggested some labor market weakness, even though demographic changes and updated Census estimates had also affected the data.

Kelly described the labor market as “not strong” but "tight," arguing that businesses continued to struggle to find workers while employees lacked the bargaining power to demand significantly higher wages.

"That's why we've got Teflon inflation here," Kelly said. "In order to get a wage-price spiral, you've got to get the wages to go up, and that's not happening."

Both economists said inflation would be the bigger driver of the Fed's next decision. Hatzius said next week's inflation report would show whether June's benign reading had been "a one-off or maybe the start of a softer trend," adding that one month of data was insufficient to draw firm conclusions.

Looking ahead, Kelly said Fed Chair Kevin Warsh would likely have to offer clearer guidance at the Jackson Hole symposium.

"You really need to communicate," Kelly said. "Uncertainty is sand in the gears of the economy."

Hatzius said policymakers were likely to continue expressing differing views ahead of the September meeting, but he expected inflation data to remain benign enough for the Fed to leave rates unchanged.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls declined by 23K in July, missing the +88K consensus and erasing the 20K increase in June, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday. What's more, June's growth was scaled back by more than half from the initial print of 57K. Unemployment slipped to 4.1% from 4.2% in June, lower than the 4.2% consensus.

Celsius jumps on report Rockstar Energy founder takes stake, wants to be CEO
data.description:
Celsius Holdings (CELH) soared 15% after a report that Rockstar Energy founder  Russ Savage has taken a stake and wants to change management after the energy drink maker's earnings miss on Thursday.

The billionaire founder of Rockstar, who sold the company to PepsiCo in 2020 for $3.85 billion, controls more than 12 million Celsius (CELH) shares, he told CNBC on Friday. 

While Savage has been talking quietly to Celsius (CELH) about changing its cost structure and marketing for over a year, he now believes new leadership is needed. 

“The CEO, the COO, the brand manager, and the marketing manager all need to be fired,” Savage, who now has a 4.7% stake in Celsius (CELH), told the business network.

He said he would like to take over as CEO to resolve the problems at the energy drink maker. 

“I’m publicly volunteering to do it,” Savage told CNBC. “The CEO has lost credibility with the investment community.”

Celsius didn’t immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

The comments come after Celsius (CELH) shares plunged 18% on Thursday after reporting Q2 revenue that was short of analysts' estimates.

nLIGHT stock falls as China-linked supply issues overshadow quarterly beat
data.description:
nLIGHT (LASR) shares fell about 21% on Friday after the laser technology company warned that China-linked supply chain disruptions would weigh on current-quarter results, overshadowing better-than-expected second-quarter earnings and revenue.

The company reported adjusted earnings of 15 cents per share for the second quarter, topping analysts' estimates by a cent. Revenue rose 33.9% year over year to $82.6M, also exceeding expectations.

For the third quarter, nLIGHT forecast revenue of $63M to $73M, compared with analysts' estimates of about $69.9M. The midpoint of its outlook includes roughly $17M of product revenue that the company had expected to ship in the quarter but now expects to recognize in future periods because of supply chain constraints."We would have guided higher had it not been for the supply chain challenges that we're seeing. And those challenges come from what appears to be China increasing scrutiny on dual-use products for defense tech products," said CEO Scott Keeney.

Executives said the delays stem from increased scrutiny of China-sourced dual-use optical components, with even a small number of unavailable parts preventing completed product shipments. The company is pursuing supplier requalification, alternative sourcing and product redesigns to mitigate the impact.

Management said demand remains strong, supported by defense programs and backlog growth, while describing its Joint Lightweight Tactical Vehicle Laser Weapon System (JLWS) program as "all systems go."

Executives cautioned that the timing of backlog conversion beyond the third quarter remains uncertain, with fourth-quarter execution dependent on resolving supply bottlenecks. The company also expects little contribution from legacy industrial cutting and welding markets during the second half of 2026.

data.title: GRAIL to face FDA advisory panel for Galleri cancer screening test
data.description:
• The US FDA's Molecular and Clinical Genetics Panel of the Medical Devices Advisory Committee will meet on Sept. 23 to offer its view on GRAIL's (GRAL) Galleri multi-cancer early detection test.
  • The company submitted a Premarket Approval application for the diagnostic on Jan. 29.
  • Grail is "designed to detect cancer-specific methylation patterns shared by many types of cancer before symptoms appear," according to GRAIL. It can detect signals from more than 50 cancers.

data.title: GRAIL to face FDA AdCom in its bid to market Galleri cancer test
data.description:
The Food and Drug Administration on Friday scheduled an advisory committee meeting to discuss the Premarket Approval application filed by GRAIL (GRAL) to seek U.S. authorization for its Galleri multi-cancer early detection test.

The Molecular and Clinical Genetics Panel of the FDA’s Medical Devices Advisory Committee is expected to meet on September 23, 2026, to review the PMA and decide whether to recommend Galleri for U.S. approval.

The blood-based test designated by the FDA as a breakthrough device is designed to detect cancer-specific signals shared by many tumors before the onset of symptoms, including those without recommended screening guidelines.

GRAIL (GRAL) submitted the PMA earlier this year based on one year of follow-up data from its U.S.-based PATHFINDER 2 study and first-year data from the NHS-Galleri trial. An analysis comparing the versions of Galleri used in those studies to the updated PMA version has also been included in the submission.

data.title: indie Semiconductor jumps on strong Q2 revenue
data.description:
Shares of indie Semiconductor (INDI) gained more than 15% on Friday after the company reported better-than-expected second-quarter revenue, while its non-GAAP EPS was in line with market estimates.

The automotive semiconductor and software solutions provider reported Q2 revenue of $64M, an increase of 24% year-over-year, beating market estimates by $1.52M, while its non-GAAP EPS of -$0.05 was in line with market expectations.

indie Semiconductor reported a Q2 non-GAAP operating loss of $8.9M, compared with $14.5M a year ago, representing continued significant progress toward achieving profitability.

“indie delivered a solid quarter of top-line growth, with revenue up 24 percent year-over-year, above the midpoint of our guidance range, demonstrating the significant strides we have made in returning to a high-growth profile,” said Donald McClymont, indie’s co-founder and chief executive officer. “Momentum continues for our 77GHz radar solution with OEMs spanning North America, Europe and China, with new application use cases expanding our addressable market. Coupled with our growing computer vision activity and our growing presence in Quantum and Physical AI, indie is well positioned to capture these rapidly emerging opportunities and drive disciplined, profitable growth.”

For the third quarter, indie expects revenue to be between $67M and $73M, compared with the market consensus of $69.91M. At the midpoint of this outlook, the company anticipates 30 percent year-over-year growth, with approximately $40M from the core business and $30M from Wuxi indie Micro.

Shares of INDI have jumped more than 13% so far this year, compared with the benchmark S&P 500’s gain of 12.6% over the same period.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway Q2 earnings on deck; look for buybacks, cash, float
data.description:
Following Warren Buffett's long tradition, Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) (BRK.A), now helmed by Greg Abel, is set to post Q2 results on Saturday at 7:00 AM Central Time (8:00 AM ET).

The Omaha, Nebraska-based investing behemoth is expected to report Q2 operating earnings of $10.8B, according to the consensus estimate, up from $10.2B in Q1. 

Investors, though, will also be focused on the company's cash and Treasury holdings, which have continued to pile up for years. At March 31, 2026, it stood at $397.4B.

Steve Check, president and chief investment officer of Check Capital Management, which holds ~$500M of Berkshire stock and ~$600M in Berkshire options, wants to see the company use more of its cash holdings for stock buybacks.

"Stock buybacks are the most natural use of the cash if the stock is priced right," he told Seeking Alpha in an interview. Buying back about $50B of stock per year would likely keep Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.B) (BRK.A) cash holdings about even, he figures. 

He was a “little disappointed” in the ~$234M of stock the company repurchased in the first quarter of the year. Check expects that to change. "My understanding is that, when we get the quarterly numbers, we're going to find out the buyback was quite significant" in Q2, he said.

Investors have curbed their expectations of using the cash hoard for any “elephant-sized” acquisitions. Buffett, who remains chairman of Berkshire, is well known for his discipline in not buying when asset valuations are rich. In  prior years, he has made plain his preference to acquire stakes in well-run publicly traded companies, rather than buy entire companies outright.

After Q2 ended, Berkshire (BRK.B) closed on what's considered a relatively small acquisition — the $6.8B purchase of homebuilder Taylor Morrison Homes.

When it comes to Berkshire Hathaway's (BRK.A) (BRK.B) operations, Check will be looking at insurance, especially the underwriting side. While the company owns a sprawling range of businesses, "insurance is certainly the engine of Berkshire," he said. Underwriting is expected to be a bit tougher this quarter, he said. "It's a bit softer market."

Q2 insurance underwriting income is expected to be $2.05B, according to the Visible Alpha consensus. That's up from. $1.72B in the prior quarter but down 19% from Q2 2025.

Check will also be looking at its insurance float, which stood at $176.9B at the end of Q1. If the company makes 4.4% on that, that's a significant number for what is essentially “free” money, he said.

For the overall operations, the money manager expects results to be "flat to up" on most subsidiaries. But neither is Check expecting blockbuster performance from the company. He calls the company a "good cornerstone… a very steady 8%-10% grower." In the past year, Berkshire B shares rose ~13%, lagging the S&P 500's 22% increase.

As for Abel's performance at the company, "it's pretty early on," Check said. Still, he's happy with the choice of Buffett's successor. "We couldn't ask for a better choice," he said. 

"I don't think Greg Abel is going to do anything dumb. He might be a little bit on the conservative side, but so is Warren Buffett, for that matter," Check said.
